summary: Marigold Pay — multi-region autoscaler thrash triggered failover cascade, high 5xx and streaming resets, urgent customer escalation
description: Issue summary: Between 2026-03-11 02:10 UTC and 2026-03-11 05:40 UTC Marigold Pay experienced elevated 5xx rates and streaming connection resets originating in eu-west. Impact: customer-facing payments workflow experienced failed NLP enrichment calls for ~3.5 hours, intermittent duplicate completions, and a billing delta caused by repeated retries. Environment: hosted (multi-tenant) with Dedicated fallback configured; Marigold is enterprise with reserved burst capacity. Immediate customer impact: order processing delays, several merchant timeouts, and an executive escalation to Support + SRE. This ticket captures the incident timeline, triage and mitigation steps, resolution, and post-incident follow-up actions including remediation, credits, and runbook updates.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Replay high-concurrency synthetic load from eu-west region with 1200 rps sustained using Marigold's prompt set
2) Configure dynamic autoscaler with default thresholds and allow capacity spillover to hosted pool
3) Observe autoscaler oscillation when GPU pool scales up/down repeatedly within 60s window
4) Inspect request routing and fallback logs for increased 502/504/5xx and streaming chunk disconnects
logs: Request IDs: r-20260311-eu-001 -> r-20260311-eu-128 (see trace links in #support-marigold Slack thread)
Gateway errors: 502/504 spikes between 02:12-03:45 UTC; median latency increased from 80ms to 420ms
Serving-runtime traces: KV cache misses rose by 92% during peak; kernel selection thrash observed on quantized variant
timeline: 2026-03-11 02:05 UTC - Marigold CS reported elevated timeouts to #support and created an urgent ticket
2026-03-11 02:12 UTC - Support confirmed 5xx spike in eu-west; paged SRE; incident declared Major
2026-03-11 02:25 UTC - SRE detected autoscaler oscillation in dedicated GPU pool, observed scale-up then rapid scale-down loops
2026-03-11 02:40 UTC - Smart-routing started failover to hosted variants; increased fanout and retry amplification observed
2026-03-11 03:10 UTC - Implemented emergency mitigation: pin Marigold traffic to static reserved nodes (manual routing override)
2026-03-11 03:35 UTC - Streaming reset frequency reduced after routing override; sustained error rate decreased by ~80%
2026-03-11 04:10 UTC - Rolled back canary kernel selection for gptx-13b-quantized-v2 which showed increased OOM/latency under burst
2026-03-11 05:00 UTC - Observed normal error rates return; monitoring for residual anomalies
2026-03-11 05:40 UTC - Incident declared mitigated; customer informed and incident response initiated
2026-03-11 12:00 UTC - Follow-up meeting with Marigold engineering and CS to share timeline and immediate actions

investigation_notes: Autoscaler behavior: thresholds set to 60% utilization with cool-down 30s. Under burst, allocation latency caused controllers to oscillate leading to temporary capacity loss.
Kernel selection canary: new kernel path for gptx-13b-quantized-v2 increased per-token compute variance and occasionally triggered memory pressure during high-concurrency bursts.

Smart-routing logic: when dedicated pool reported capacity errors, routing policy triggered immediate failover to hosted variants without staged ramping, causing request fanout and retry amplification.
Billing exposure: repeated retries and duplicate completions during failover window contributed to a measurable billing delta for Marigold (preliminary estimate ~+7%).
resolution_notes: 1) Emergency manual routing override to static reserved nodes for Marigold traffic (completed 2026-03-11 03:10 UTC).
2) Reverted canary kernel selection for gptx-13b-quantized-v2 to stable kernel (2026-03-11 04:10 UTC).
3) Adjusted autoscaler cool-down and scale step to reduce oscillation (temporary config bump applied 2026-03-11 04:00 UTC; permanent change merged later).
4) Applied a staged failover policy to smart-routing to avoid full fanout on capacity errors (policy change deployed 2026-03-12).
5) Issued interim statement to the customer and scheduled post-incident review and billing reconciliation.
followup_actions: Action 1: Update autoscaler runbook with guidance for bursty traffic patterns and add test cases to CI (owner: infra-scaling team, ETA: 2026-03-21)
Action 2: Create canary criteria checklist for kernel rollouts including stress test under synthetic burst (owner: runtime team, ETA: 2026-03-18)
Action 3: Add staged-failover guard to smart-routing with configurable fanout cap per-customer to prevent retry amplification (owner: routing team, ETA: 2026-03-19)
Action 4: Finance & Support to complete billing reconciliation with Marigold and communicate credit by 2026-03-20 (owner: Finance, ETA: 2026-03-20)
Action 5: Run a joint chaos test with Marigold on a scheduled maintenance window to validate mitigations (owner: Solutions Eng, proposed date: 2026-04-02)
Action 6: Publish a concise postmortem in Confluence and link it to this ticket (owner: incident lead, ETA: 2026-03-15)
Action 7: Add an entry to Customer Status Page playbook for rapid notification templates (owner: CS ops, ETA: 2026-03-17)
